items.bold: IRAN UPDATED PROPOSAL via Pakistan — delivered to US. Brent settled $108.17 (-2%) on Friday.
items.text: CNBC confirmed: Iran sent an updated peace proposal to Pakistan mediators Friday. Pakistani officials confirmed it was delivered to the US. The "not satisfied" language is softer than "unacceptable" — suggesting Iran's updated proposal has moved somewhat but not enough.

items.text: Axios confirmed: CENTCOM has prepared a "short and powerful" wave of strikes plan to break the negotiating deadlock. Trump was briefed at the White House by Admiral Cooper (CENTCOM) AND Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Having the Joint Chiefs Chair in the room signals the most serious military planning process of the war so far. No decision made yet — but the plan is ready to execute.

items.text: Bloomberg confirmed: US is pitching allies on a joint naval force to secure Hormuz — an active enforcement force against Iran's blockade, distinct from the Northwood mine-clearing conference. Separately: Iran activated air defenses around Tehran Thursday night to counter reconnaissance drones ("small drones, micro-UAVs" per Iranian state media). Cause of drone incursion unconfirmed. Either a US/Israeli reconnaissance mission or an internal test.

items.bold: GOLDMAN SACHS 4th upgrade: Brent $90 Q4 2026. Inventories at RECORD draw 11-12 Mbpd. Gulf output -14.5 Mbpd.
items.text: Goldman Sachs (April 26 note, confirmed): fourth Brent upgrade since war began — Q4 2026 forecast now $90 (from $80 previously). The track: $66→$71→$80→$90, each revision tied to a longer assumed Hormuz disruption. April global oil inventories drawing at 11-12 Mbpd — fastest pace on record since satellite tracking began. Gulf crude production collapsed to 11.9 Mbpd from pre-war 26.4 Mbpd — a 14.5 Mbpd hit. Goldman now sees market swinging from 1.8 Mbpd surplus in 2025 to a 9.6 Mbpd deficit in Q2 2026. Even at the Q4 $90 forecast: Brent stays 38% above pre-war for the rest of 2026.

military.t: TRUE WAR COST: $50 BILLION — Double Pentagon's Public Figure. Munitions Depletion Key Gap.
military.d: CBS News (1 day ago) confirmed: the true price tag of the Iran war is closer to $50 billion, per US officials familiar with internal assessments — roughly double the $25B the Pentagon cited publicly to Congress. "Much of the gap is accounted for by munitions that have been used and need to be replaced." Pentagon: $25B. Democratic senators: "probably less than a quarter of the true cost." CBS/officials: $50B. The munitions gap directly validates Vance's privately expressed concern (The Atlantic) that the war is depleting US weapons stockpiles. At $50B over 64 days: approximately $780M/day in true war costs. The $50B figure will accelerate congressional pressure and the Murkowski AUMF May 11 deadline.

military.t: IRAN UPDATED PROPOSAL via Pakistan — Brent -2% to $108.17. Trump: "Not Satisfied."
military.d: CNBC and Bloomberg confirmed: Iran sent an updated peace proposal to Pakistan mediators Friday. Pakistani officials confirmed delivery to US. Brent -2% to $108.17, WTI $101.94 (-3%) on hopes. IRNA confirmed relayed via Pakistan — did not specify nuclear or Hormuz specifics. Trump: "Iran wants to make a deal, but I'm not satisfied with it. Iran wants to make a deal because they have no military left." "Not satisfied" is softer than "unacceptable" (previous proposal language) — suggests the updated proposal may have moved marginally toward US requirements. WH counterproposal still not delivered. Pakistan and Oman back-channels remain active.

military.t: TRUMP AI-GUN POST: "Iran Better Get Smart Soon!" No More Mr. Nice Guy.
military.d: CNBC confirmed: Trump posted an AI-generated image of himself holding a gun with explosions and "NO MORE MR. NICE GUY" on Truth Social, alongside: "Iran can't get their act together. They don't know how to sign a nonnuclear deal. They better get smart soon!" Most aggressive public Trump threat since the war began. Posted on the same day CENTCOM briefed him on "short and powerful" strike options. The visual messaging is deliberate — maximum resolve to Iran's leadership at a moment when diplomatic channels are stalled. The AI-gun post is designed to pressure Iran into modifying its nuclear position before the WH counterproposal is delivered. Calibrated brinkmanship, not a declaration of military action.

military.t: US GAS $4.39/Gallon Friday — Up 34 Cents from Week Ago. Domestic Pressure on Trump Rising.
military.d: CBS News confirmed: average US gas hit $4.39/gallon Friday (AAA) — up 9 cents from Thursday, 34 cents from week ago and month ago. Highest since 2022. Iran war directly hitting American households at the pump. Gas prices up ~27% since war began. Combined with grocery inflation (fertiliser supply disruption), Americans experiencing the Iran war in daily costs. This domestic pressure is a key driver of Trump's stated desire for a deal — on his terms. Trump: "We've already won. I want to win by a bigger margin." The $4.39 figure creates political urgency for resolution even as Trump maintains the blockade.

military.t: Goldman Sachs: Hormuz 4% of Normal. UAE OPEC Exit "Gradual" — No Near-Term Offset.
military.d: CNBC confirmed: Goldman Sachs estimates exports through Hormuz fallen to 4% of normal. Bank separately noted UAE OPEC departure boost to global supply is "likely to materialise more gradually over the medium term rather than offsetting near-term tightness." Key nuance: UAE OPEC exit (widely seen as partial supply positive) will NOT help near-term. Goldman raised Brent forecast to $90 late 2026 — normalisation only by end-June at earliest. Inventories drawing at record 11-12M bbl/day in April. CNBC analyst Perkins (Skylar Capital): "We're kind of far apart from a deal, and maybe hostilities or a little bit more time is needed to open up the Strait of Hormuz." Product markets — diesel especially — significantly more strained than crude.

assessment.body:
Saturday 6:30 PM IST. Day 64. The weekend bringing clarity on where the war stands.

THE IRAN PROPOSAL — WHAT WE KNOW
• Iran submitted an updated proposal to Pakistan mediators on Friday
• Pakistani officials confirmed: delivered to the US
• IRNA confirmed: content not disclosed on Hormuz or nuclear
• Brent fell 2% to $108.17 on proposal hope
• Trump: "not satisfied" — softer than "unacceptable" (previous proposal)
• The gap may be narrowing — but is not closed

THE MILITARY REALITY
• CENTCOM prepared "short and powerful" strikes plan (Axios confirmed)
• Trump briefed by Cooper (CENTCOM) AND Caine (Joint Chiefs Chair)
• Joint Chiefs Chair in room = highest-level military planning of the war
• No decision made — but plan is ready to execute immediately
• US also pitching allies on joint naval force for Hormuz enforcement

THE OIL MARKET — GOLDMAN'S FOURTH UPGRADE
• Goldman Sachs Q4 2026 Brent: $90 (4th upgrade since war: $66→$71→$80→$90)
• April inventories drawing at 11-12 Mbpd — fastest on record
• Gulf crude output: 11.9 Mbpd vs 26.4 Mbpd pre-war — 14.5 Mbpd collapse
• Goldman: market swings to 9.6 Mbpd DEFICIT in Q2 2026
• Even at $90 Q4 2026: Brent stays 38% above pre-war for rest of year
• Brent currently $107-110 Saturday — easing from $126 peak

INDIA'S EQUITY MARKET — CAUTIOUS RECOVERY EXPECTED
• Nifty targets cut 3.8% — from 29,899 pre-war to 28,747 now
• Morgan Stanley: Sensex 95,000 by December 2026 (base case)
• HDFC Securities: nearing end of 18-month correction cycle
• Goldman sector strategy: buy financials, staples, telecom; avoid autos, durables
• India markets reopen Monday 9:15 AM IST
• State election results May 4 = additional domestic catalyst

VERDICT: Day 64 closes with the West Asia War's diplomatic and military tracks running at maximum intensity — simultaneously. Iran is submitting proposals. CENTCOM is briefing the President on strikes. Goldman is revising oil forecasts upward for the fourth time. And India watches from the sidelines, markets closed for the weekend, waiting for Monday morning to price two weeks of war developments. The Takshashila Geospatial Bulletin's new analysis of the "new logic of chokepoint control" frames it well: Hormuz is no longer a binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest — and the contest shows no signs of resolution.

featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
